title: Did they answer? Subjective acts and intents in conversational discourse

bias_targets.methodology: Eliciting crowdsourced annotators' subjective sentiments (negative, neutral, positive) towards witnesses and politicians in U.S. congressional hearings, and analyzing how these prior beliefs correlate with their interpretations of the speakers' conversational acts and intents (e.g., judging a response as sincere vs. deceptive). The study evaluates this bias by incorporating annotator sentiment ratings as features in a transformer-based multi-label classifier to predict subjective discourse interpretations.
